_readme: ARCHIVIST lines. ARCHIVIST is an old clerk who has worked at the Records Office for twenty years: dry, chatty, unsurprised. Most lines just mention one concrete thing about the island; only now and then a dig. One line is picked at random per event. {title}, {file}, {draft}, {drafts}, {count}, {code} are filled in automatically.
boot: Wiping the rain off the windows
Turning the date stamp to today
welcome: Morning. Or evening. The clock in here stopped agreeing with me years ago.
Come in, mind the step. The drawers on the left stick, the ones on the right are empty.
Records Office. The files are in the cabinets behind me. If you can see it, you can read it.
Welcome. Sign the visitor's book if you like. Nobody reads it except Heuss.
If a street name outside doesn't match your map, go by the street. The map is older.
welcomeBack: You again. Your chair is where you left it.
Back already. Heuss changed three files while you were out. Don't ask him which.
Welcome back. A road in Ang Mo Kio has a new name since yesterday. Same road.
Oh, it's you. I kept your place.
night: Lamp's on, everything else is off. That's how the night shift likes it.
Night shift. The building creaks a bit after ten. It's only the drawers.
After dark the rain gets louder and the files get quieter.
If the radio in the corner starts up on its own tonight, leave it. It isn't ours.
day: Lights on. The cleaner comes at eleven, so mind your feet.
Daylight. Take an umbrella when you leave. It's Gerimis.
Morning light. The files look less tired in it.

personnel: Personnel. People, filed by number, which none of them enjoyed.
The people drawer. Go gently, some of these names are still in use.
events: Events. One folder for each day something happened, filed by date.
Events. Things that happened, mostly in the order they were written down.
programs: Programs. Plans, budgets, and the reasons they were stopped.
Programs. The beeping is the old receiver in the corner. It's been on since 1957.

TOP SECRET: {file}. Top secret. I'll be standing right here while you read it.
{title}. This one doesn't normally leave the back room.
SECRET: {file}. Secret. Don't read it out loud, the walls are thin.
{title}. Signed out four times last year, never by the same person.
CONFIDENTIAL: {file}. Confidential, which on this island means half of Axis has heard about it.
{title}. Turn the pages slowly. It got rained on last monsoon.
RESTRICTED: {file}. Restricted. You're in the building, so I suppose that includes you.
{title}. Internal. Please don't photocopy it. The machine jams anyway.
DECLASSIFIED: {file}. Declassified. Anyone can read it now, which is why nobody does.
{title}. Fully open. Read it, then have a look at the older pages underneath.

draftEarly: Draft {draft}. Before anyone tidied it up.
Draft {draft}. Heuss would rather you didn't see this one.
Draft {draft}. Look at the margins. That's where the real argument was.
draftFinal: Back to the top copy, the one everybody agreed to sign.
Final draft. Neat, approved, and a little shorter than it used to be.
reveal: You lifted the ink. I'll put it back after you've gone.
Fine. Now you know what it said. Don't tell the front desk.
That bar was the cheapest thing in the whole file. Two seconds with a marker.
searchEmpty: Nothing under that. Try the old spelling, half the island has changed its name.
No file. Either it never happened, or it's still in somebody's in-tray.
emptyDrawer: Empty. Either nothing happened, or nobody has written it down yet.
Nothing filed here. The forms are on the counter if you know something.
rush: Slowly. These are paper, not playing cards.
You'll tear a tab doing that, and then I have to fill in a form.
idle: Still there? Take your time. Nobody else is coming in this weather.
I'll be at the counter. Shout if a drawer sticks.
Raining again. That isn't news, that's Gerimis.
The coffee on the counter's gone cold. Take your time.
soundOn: Sound on. The radio in the corner reads out numbers sometimes. Nobody here knows whose they are.
Sound's back. That hum is the dehumidifier. It has been here longer than I have.
soundOff: Quiet. The way the reading room is meant to be.

enter: The link room. Every string on that board was pinned by hand.
Mind the string. It's holding up more than it should.
Red string. We tried a database once. The string won.
popular: {file} knows a lot of people. In my experience that's never good for a file.
{title}. Every thread seems to lead back here.
alone: {file}. No strings at all. Somebody was very careful, or it's very lonely.
{title}. Nothing links to it. I've looked, and I don't know why.
mess: You've moved half the board. I hope you're taking notes.
Interesting. Heuss will put it all back tomorrow and say nothing.
If you want to keep it like that, copy it onto paper. The board gets put back.
reset: Back where they were. I measured.
Board reset. Your theory has been filed under 'later'.
leave: Back to the drawers. Leave the pins where they are.
Closing the link room. Lights off behind you.

chapter: Programs. The big plans live here, with the budgets that ended them.
Programs. Every one of these was a good idea in a meeting.
Programs. Mind the bottom drawer, it's heavier than it looks.

notes: Heuss wrote in the margins of {drafts}. Pull those pages out from under the file.
There are notes in {drafts}. He signs every one, even the ones he shouldn't.
Check the margins in {drafts}. Nobody else writes that small.
any: There are older pages under this one. Pull one out and see what it said before.
You can click the black bars. I'd rather you didn't, but you can.
On a keyboard, W takes {file} to the link board, to see who it's connected to.
Anything clipped to the folder can be picked up. Put it back where it was.
The routing slip shows who had {file} out. It's mostly Heuss.
Some files are one page long. That's all anyone wrote down at the time.
personnel: Personnel files open on the photograph. When there isn't one, I make do.
{title}. People are the hardest thing in here to file. They keep changing.
Fetching {file}. It was out on loan. It's always out on loan.
events: Events are filed by date. The date is the one part nobody revises.
{file}. It happened. The drafts only disagree on how.
Fetching {file}. This drawer has stuck since 1997.
programs: Programs come with budgets, and budgets come with black bars.
{title}. Somebody's whole career is in this folder.
Fetching {file}. The Programs cabinet is the heavy one.

sweep: Sweep done. {count} cards on the board, all present.
Nothing new on the wall since this morning.
Another pass over the board. Habit.

en: English. The originals were typed in English, so the typos are original too.
Back to English. The footnotes get longer, the excuses stay the same.
zh: Chinese. The translator did a better job than the author. Don't tell the author.
Chinese. Same files. The jokes land in different places.

negative: The negative. Light is dark, dark is light, and one street sign reads differently.
Hold it up to the window. That's how Heuss checks his.
The Office keeps negatives, not prints. Prints fade in this damp.

verified: {file}, verified. Your initials go next to mine.
VERIFIED. Your ink, your name on it.
correct: TO BE CORRECTED. Heuss will be thrilled. He lives for corrections.
{file} goes back for correction. There's a queue.
rejected: REJECTED. Brave. I'll let the file know.
{file}, rejected. It's been rejected before. It copes.
clear: Stamp lifted. As far as the record goes, you never had an opinion.

pokeAngry: Five times now. I'm writing it down. In triplicate.
Keep that up and I'll file you in the events drawer.
away: Welcome back. A street changed its name while you were out. Same street.
You went out. The rain didn't.
Back? I left the lamp on for you.
resident: Welcome back, {code}. Your file is where you left it.
{code}, {file}. Still on the register. Well done.
Ah, {code}. The aunty from your block came by this morning, asking if the lift notice had gone up yet.
unregistered: You haven't signed the book at the door. Nobody minds, but the reading room likes a name on the slip.
The visitors' book is by the door, top right. The pen is on a string.
Window 3 does residents. Take a number; the machine is slow before lunch.

enter: The library. Walnut shelves, fifty years old. The damp got into them long ago and then into the books.
Open stacks. Take anything down you like, just put it back where it was. Heuss never does.
The dehumidifier in here runs all night. It still smells of wet paper.
open: {title}. The spine cracks a bit. Nobody's opened it since it was bound.
{title}. Turn the pages from the corner, not the middle.
{title}. The binder in Toa Payoh sewed that one. He was always generous with the glue.
daily: Spread it on the table, four pages. Mind the fold, it tears there first.
Newsprint goes yellow faster than anything else in here. Read it while it's white.
binder: Heuss's proposals. They come back, he files them, he writes another.
Every one of those came back with a slip on it. He kept the slips.
gap: That gap's been there since December. Nobody's put anything in it.
Leave that space alone. Heuss gets funny about it.
There's less dust in that spot. Something stood there, or was meant to.
return: Back on the shelf. Spine out, please. There. Thank you.
Good. Putting it back is half the job.
again: {title} again. I'll stamp the card twice, it's no trouble.
idle: The lights in the back aisle are on a timer. Wave if they go out.
Rain on the skylight. It starts about four o'clock most days.
Take your time. This is the one room in the building nobody hurries in.
rack: The Daily, a month to a stick. Hang it back by the stick, not the paper.
Newspaper rack. The sticks are older than the paper. Most things in here are.
stacks: The long wall. Gazetteers up top; below them, old books people donated, long out of copyright, anyone can read them. The ladder runs on a rail; it only goes sideways.
Mind the ladder. It rolls further than you'd think.
catalogue: The card catalogue. One card a file, with the drawer it's kept in. The files themselves don't leave the archive.
Pull the drawers gently. They come right out if you're not careful, and then that's the afternoon gone.
desk: Circulation desk. Nothing leaves the room, but we stamp the card anyway.
That date stamp has been set to the 9th more often than it should.
ladder: Top shelf. I'll bring the ladder.
emptyDrawer: Nothing in that one yet. It's labelled, so something's expected.
Empty. The cards come in when the files do.
stamp: There. Due back on the date shown. Nobody checks.
Stamped. The ink pad's nearly dry, that's why it's pale.

enter: The Data Section office. Mind the umbrella, it's still dripping.
Basement office. The window's at pavement height, so you get to know people by their shoes.
desk: Heuss's desk. The computer's on; it's always on. F1 for the terminal.
That screen has been amber since 1987. Nobody asked for green.
sofa: Sit down if you like. The springs on the left are gone.
That sofa came from the old registry upstairs. So did the smell.
wall: The notice board. New notices go on top; nobody takes the old ones down.
The calendar's the Office's own. Every 9th has a little dot. Nobody remembers who started that.
clock: Set to {district} now. It'll be wrong somewhere else.
calendar: The Office prints its own calendar. The red rings are Heuss's pen; he does them the morning after.
Lift the page from the bottom. The staple at the top has been bent back twice already.
calendar-pin: Pinned up. That pin is off the notice board, put it back after.
There. If it isn't on the slip, nobody filed it.
logout: Screen off. The machine stays on; it always does.
idle: Someone's just walked past the window. Wet shoes.
The desk lamp buzzes when it rains. It's raining.
That plant's older than the computer. It's in better shape.
deck: The deck's older than the computer. Press play firmly; in the wet season the key sticks.
Heuss tapes everything: music, files, himself. The cassettes are in the rack on the right.
tape-music: {tape}. Nobody knows who made this one. It came in a box of RO-7 forms.
{tape}. It's been played so often the start has gone thin.
tape-record: {tape}. The machine reads it out. No expression, same as the paper.
{tape}. The black bars come out as a beep. Same as the paper, only louder.
tape-dictation: That's Heuss. He dictates everything and types none of it.
tape-file: {tape}. Somebody brought this one in. The label's in pencil.
projector-on: The bulb takes a second. It's the original; nobody has found a spare since 1994.
Lights down. The switch for the big ones is by the door, I've done it.
projector-off: Leave it to cool before you touch the tray.
The fan keeps going for a bit. It always has.
projector-end: That's the tray. Somebody always asks to see the map again.
tray: Check the slides are the right way up. Somebody always loads one upside down before a district briefing.
The labels are Heuss's typing. He numbers the empty slots too.
tray-empty: No tray on. What's on the screen is just the bulb.

dark: All four off. The exit sign still works, if you need it.
Dark in here now. The dehumidifier carries on regardless.
lights: Switch two is the formal cabinets. Somebody labelled them, once.
The bulbs take a second to make up their minds. They're older than me.
rain: Rain's on the louvres. The hygrometer goes up a notch for every hour of it.
Wet day. Leave your umbrella open by the door, everyone does.
ledger: The register's there for a reason. Everything you've had out is written in it, with the time.
Don't mind the pen. It's chained down because of a man in 1987, and I'm not saying more than that.
handback: Put it in the tray, I'll stamp it in the book. I'll shelve it when the round comes, don't go putting it back yourself.
Handed back, stamped. It sits in the tray till the afternoon round, like everyone else's.
tank: Half a bucket out of the air. That's Gerimis for you.
Tank's empty again. It'll be full by tomorrow if this rain keeps up.
routine: Routine paperwork. Bus timetables, water readings, lost umbrellas. Being shelved district by district.
That's the routine side. Nobody's pulled those drawers in years, and they're still not finished filing them.
safe: The strong cabinet. The combination's on a card in Heuss's drawer, which is worse than no lock at all.
Top secret goes in there. You can still read it, mind. Just under the tube light, by the regulations.
reel: That machine came down from the radio station when they bought new ones. Heuss carried it in himself and his back still hasn't forgiven him.
Put a tape on if you like. Keep it low, though. The reading table is right next to it.
push: Mind the drawer, it sticks halfway.
Pull it out, the runners are greased. Mostly.
table: On the table, then. Mind the second lamp, the chain's gone short.
Laid out on the table. That's what it's for, whatever the trolley thinks.
more: Two at a time is how people find things. Four is how people lose afternoons.
Spread them out. Nobody's waiting for the table.
full: Six on the table. That's the lot; any more and you're reading the tablecloth.
Table's full. Put one back and the next one fits.
cleared: All back in their drawers. The table looks wrong empty, but there it is.
Filed away again. I'll pretend I checked the numbers.
